proofs.proof_tex:
By \(\text{ass:compact-treatment}\), \(D_1,D_2\in I\) almost surely, and hence
\[
 |Z|=|D_2-D_1|\leq \operatorname{diam}(I)
 \qquad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]
By \(\text{ass:no-stayers}\), \(|Z|>0\) almost surely.  Consequently
\[
 0<A=E_P|Z|\leq \operatorname{diam}(I)<\infty.
\]
Moreover, \(\text{ass:observed-integrability}\) gives
\(E_P|\Delta Y|\leq E_P(|Y_1|+|Y_2|)<\infty\).  Since
\(|S|=1\) almost surely under the no-stayer condition, the definition of \(T\)
therefore gives \(|T|<\infty\).  Thus every ratio below is well defined.

First take \(Q\in\mathfrak Q(P)\), where \(\mathfrak Q(P)\) is the class in
\(\text{def:legal-completion-class}\), and write \(m=m_Q\).  Consistency, which
is one of the defining conditions of that class, implies
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Delta Y
 &=Y_2^Q(D_2)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\\
 &=\{Y_2^Q(D_2)-Y_2^Q(D_1)\}
   +\{Y_2^Q(D_1)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The simultaneous clause in \(\text{ass:conditional-parallel-trends}\) supplies
one \(Q\)-full event on which the asserted conditional-mean equality holds for
every \(d\in X_0\).  Since \(D_1=X\in X_0\) almost surely by the definition of
\(X_0\), evaluating the jointly measurable versions on the random diagonal
\(d=X\) is legitimate and yields
\[
 E_Q\!\left[Y_2^Q(D_1)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\mid X,Z\right]
 =E_Q\!\left[Y_2^Q(X)-Y_1^Q(X)\mid X\right]
 =m(X).
\]
Taking conditional expectations in the preceding decomposition, using the
observed-law match in \(\text{def:legal-completion-class}\), and using the
declared support version \(g\), gives
\[
 g(x,z)-m(x)
 =E_Q\!\left[Y_2^Q(D_2)-Y_2^Q(D_1)\mid X=x,Z=z\right]
\]
for \(P_{XZ}\)-almost every \((x,z)\).  The condition
\(\text{ass:mean-movement-bound}\) therefore implies
\[
 |g(x,z)-m(x)|\leq K|z|
 \qquad P_{XZ}\text{-almost everywhere}.
\]
The map \((x,z)\mapsto |g(x,z)-m(x)|-K|z|\) is continuous on \(H\): continuity
of \(g\) follows from \(\text{ass:continuous-regression}\), while
\(m\in C(X_0)\) is part of \(\text{def:legal-completion-class}\).  If this map
were positive at a point of \(H=\operatorname{supp}_P(X,Z)\), continuity would
make it positive on a relatively open neighborhood of that point, and the
definition of support would give that neighborhood positive \(P_{XZ}\)-mass.
This would contradict the almost-everywhere inequality.  Hence
\[
 |g(x,z)-m(x)|\leq K|z|
 \qquad\text{for every }(x,z)\in H.
\]
The trend bound and the global \(L\)-Lipschitz condition are also defining
conditions of \(\mathfrak Q(P)\).  Comparing these three properties with
\(\text{def:feasible-trend-class}\) proves \(m\in\mathcal C_P\), and in
particular
\[
 \mathfrak Q(P)\neq\varnothing\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing.
\]

The same decomposition relates the causal estimand to the observed law rather
than defining that relationship.  By the definition of \(\theta(Q)\), the
diagonal conditional-mean equality just established, iterated expectations,
and \(\text{def:signed-functional}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 A\theta(Q)
 &=E_Q\!\left[S\{Y_2^Q(D_2)-Y_2^Q(D_1)\}\right]\\
 &=E_P[S\Delta Y]
   -E_Q\!\left[S\{Y_2^Q(D_1)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\}\right]\\
 &=T-E_P[Sm(X)]\\
 &=T-\int_{X_0}m(x)\,d\nu_P(x)\\
 &=T-J_P(m).
\end{aligned}
\]
The signed integral is finite because \(m\) is bounded and \(\nu_P\) is a
finite signed measure.  Since \(m\in\mathcal C_P\),
\(\text{def:waoss-set}\) now shows
\[
 \{\theta(Q):Q\in\mathfrak Q(P)\}\subseteq\Theta(P).
\]

For the reverse inclusion, fix an arbitrary \(u\in\mathcal C_P\).  Retain on
the same probability space the observed vector with law \(P\), and use the
construction in \(\text{def:affine-lift}\): on \(\{Z\neq0\}\), set
\[
 b_u=\frac{g(X,Z)-u(X)}{Z},
\]
and set \(b_u=0\) on the \(P\)-null event \(\{Z=0\}\).  The variables involved
are Borel measurable because \(g\) and \(u\) are continuous on their compact
supports.  The support obstacle in \(\text{def:feasible-trend-class}\) gives
\[
 |b_u|\leq K\qquad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]
Define, simultaneously for every \(d\in I\),
\[
 Y_1^{Q_u}(d)=Y_1+b_u(d-D_1),
 \qquad
 Y_2^{Q_u}(d)=Y_2+b_u(d-D_2).
\]
These are jointly measurable one-argument static schedules.  At the realized
treatments they satisfy, pointwise,
\[
 Y_1^{Q_u}(D_1)=Y_1,
 \qquad
 Y_2^{Q_u}(D_2)=Y_2.
\]
Thus consistency holds and the entire joint observed law, not only selected
moments, remains \(P\).  For every fixed \(d\in I\), compactness of \(I\), the
bound on \(b_u\), and \(\text{ass:observed-integrability}\) imply
\[
 |Y_t^{Q_u}(d)|\leq |Y_t|+K\operatorname{diam}(I),
 \qquad E_{Q_u}|Y_t^{Q_u}(d)|<\infty.
\]
Also, for all \(d,d'\in I\),
\[
 |Y_t^{Q_u}(d)-Y_t^{Q_u}(d')|
 =|b_u|\,|d-d'|
 \leq K|d-d'|,
\]
so each period schedule is individually \(K\)-Lipschitz.

Direct subtraction gives, on one common full-probability event and
simultaneously for every \(d\in I\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 Y_2^{Q_u}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u}(d)
 &=\Delta Y+b_u(D_1-D_2)\\
 &=\Delta Y-b_uZ\\
 &=\Delta Y-g(X,Z)+u(X).
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \(g(X,Z)=E_P[\Delta Y\mid X,Z]\), one may choose conditional-expectation
versions, for every \(d\in I\), satisfying
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_{Q_u}[Y_2^{Q_u}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u}(d)\mid X,Z]&=u(X),\\
 E_{Q_u}[Y_2^{Q_u}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u}(d)\mid X]&=u(X).
\end{aligned}
\]
The same two versions work for every \(d\), so the stronger all-\(I\)
simultaneous parallel-trends equality, and hence the required diagonal clause,
holds.  In particular, the second displayed version gives
\(m_{Q_u}(x)=u(x)\) on \(X_0\).  Its level and global Lipschitz restrictions
follow from \(u\in\mathcal C_P\).

The period-two causal movement under this lift is
\[
 Y_2^{Q_u}(D_2)-Y_2^{Q_u}(D_1)
 =b_uZ=g(X,Z)-u(X).
\]
It is integrable because it is bounded in absolute value by \(K|Z|\), and,
being measurable with respect to \((X,Z)\), it satisfies
\[
 \left|E_{Q_u}[Y_2^{Q_u}(D_2)-Y_2^{Q_u}(D_1)\mid X,Z]\right|
 =|b_uZ|\leq K|Z|.
\]
We have therefore checked every member property in
\(\text{def:legal-completion-class}\), so \(Q_u\in\mathfrak Q(P)\).  This also
proves
\(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\Rightarrow\mathfrak Q(P)\neq\varnothing\).
Finally, by the causal definition and iterated expectations,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \theta(Q_u)
 &=\frac{E_P[S\{g(X,Z)-u(X)\}]}{A}\\
 &=\frac{T-J_P(u)}{A},
\end{aligned}
\]
because \(E_P[Sg(X,Z)]=E_P[S\Delta Y]=T\).  Since \(u\) was arbitrary, every
point of \(\Theta(P)\) is attained by a legal full-data law, whereas the first
half of the proof excludes every other value.  This proves both nonemptiness
equivalence and the asserted sharp set equality.

No step used \(\text{ass:marginal-quasi-stayers}\).  The proof instead used the
finite mean-movement bound, the bounded globally Lipschitz trend, the continuous
support version of \(g\), and the simultaneous diagonal clause exactly where
indicated.  These are the extra restrictions built into the sensitivity class
\(\mathfrak Q(P)\).  Accordingly, the set equality just proved is a
characterization of that class and supplies no equality with, or upward
transfer to, the unrestricted published completion class.

The first rectangle in \(\text{def:continuous-hole-witness}\) has area
\(1/2\) and density \(2p_{\circ}\), so it has probability \(p_{\circ}\).  The
second rectangle also has area \(1/2\) and density \(2(1-p_{\circ})\), so it
has probability \(1-p_{\circ}\).  Since \(p_{\circ}\in(0,1)\), this density is
bounded and has a strictly positive constant value on each rectangle.  The
observed outcomes are identically zero and hence uniformly bounded.  Absolute
continuity gives \(P^{\circ}(Z=0)=0\).  The second rectangle contains a set of
positive Lebesgue measure with \(|Z|\leq\eta\) for every \(\eta>0\), and hence
\[
 P^{\circ}(|Z|\leq\eta)>0
 \qquad\text{for every }\eta>0,
\]
which verifies \(\text{ass:marginal-quasi-stayers}\).  In contrast, for every
\(x\in[-1,0)\), the conditional support of \(Z\) is \([1/2,1]\), so
\[
 P^{\circ}(|Z|\leq\eta\mid X=x)=0
 \qquad(0<\eta<1/2).
\]
The marginal density of \(X\) on \([-1,0]\) is \(p_{\circ}\); therefore this
failure region has \(P_X^{\circ}\)-probability \(p_{\circ}\).

Fix a finite \(c\in\mathbb R\) and consider \(Q_c^{\circ}\) from
\(\text{def:source-recession-ray}\).  On the first rectangle,
\(|\phi(X)|\leq1/2\leq |Z|\), while on the second rectangle \(\phi(X)=0\).
Thus, outside the null event \(\{Z=0\}\),
\[
 \left|\frac{c\phi(X)}{Z}\right|\leq |c|.
\]
Because \(D_1,D_2,d\in[-2,2]\), both schedules in that definition are bounded
in absolute value by \(4|c|\) for every fixed \(d\).  They are consequently
integrable and affine in \(d\), with the everywhere finite derivative
\(-c\phi(X)/Z\).  At the realized treatments,
\[
 Y_1^{Q_c^{\circ}}(D_1)=0=Y_1,
 \qquad
 Y_2^{Q_c^{\circ}}(D_2)=0=Y_2.
\]
Consistency therefore holds and the complete observed vector retains law
\(P^{\circ}\).

For every \(d\in[-2,2]\), direct subtraction gives, on the same event for all
\(d\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 Y_2^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)-Y_1^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)
 &=-\frac{c\phi(X)}{Z}\{(d-D_2)-(d-X)\}\\
 &=c\phi(X).
\end{aligned}
\]
The right-hand side is measurable with respect to \(X\).  Hence one may choose
versions such that, simultaneously for every \(d\in[-2,2]\),
\[
 E_{Q_c^{\circ}}[Y_2^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)-Y_1^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)\mid X,Z]
 =c\phi(X)
 =E_{Q_c^{\circ}}[Y_2^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)-Y_1^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)\mid X].
\]
This verifies the parallel-trends condition in
\(\text{def:published-source-completion-class}\), and in fact verifies the
stronger common-event equality over all of \([-2,2]\).  Together with the
observed support, consistency, integrability, and derivative checks above, it
proves
\[
 Q_c^{\circ}\in\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{src}}(P^{\circ})
 \qquad\text{for every finite }c\in\mathbb R.
\]

The period-two causal movement is
\[
 Y_2^{Q_c^{\circ}}(D_2)-Y_2^{Q_c^{\circ}}(D_1)=-c\phi(X).
\]
On the first rectangle \(S=1\).  On the second rectangle \(Z\) is conditionally
uniform on the symmetric interval \([-1/4,1/4]\), and in any case
\(\phi(X)=0\) there.  It follows that
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_{P^{\circ}}[S\phi(X)]
 &=p_{\circ}\int_{-1}^{0}\min\{-x,1/2\}\,dx\\
 &=\frac{3p_{\circ}}{8}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The denominator is strictly positive and equals
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_{P^{\circ}}|Z|
 &=p_{\circ}\,E[Z\mid Z\in[1/2,1]]
   +(1-p_{\circ})E[|Z|\mid Z\in[-1/4,1/4]]\\
 &=\frac{3p_{\circ}}4+\frac{1-p_{\circ}}8
 =\frac{1+5p_{\circ}}8.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore the causal definition of \(\theta\), rather than a definition by an
observed functional, gives
\[
 \theta(Q_c^{\circ})
 =\frac{-cE_{P^{\circ}}[S\phi(X)]}{E_{P^{\circ}}|Z|}
 =-\frac{3cp_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}}.
\]
The coefficient \(3p_{\circ}/(1+5p_{\circ})\) is strictly positive.  Letting
\(c\) range over \(\mathbb R\) proves
\[
 \mathbb R\subseteq
 \{\theta(Q):Q\in\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{src}}(P^{\circ})\}.
\]
Conversely, the definition of the source completion class requires the causal
movement entering \(\theta(Q)\) to be integrable, and the denominator displayed
above is positive, so each such \(\theta(Q)\) is a finite real number.  The
reverse inclusion follows, establishing equality with \(\mathbb R\).

It remains to calculate the bounded-sensitivity stage.  Since \(\Delta Y=0\)
under \(P^{\circ}\), its continuous conditional-mean support version is
\(g=0\).  Set \(K=L=M=1\).  Every \(u\in\mathcal C_{P^{\circ}}\) satisfies
\(u(x)=0\) on \([0,1]\), because \((x,0)\in H\) there and the obstacle in
\(\text{def:feasible-trend-class}\) at \(z=0\) has zero radius.  In particular
\(u(0)=0\).  On \([-1,0]\), the support contains \((x,1/2)\), so the obstacle
gives \(|u(x)|\leq1/2\); global one-Lipschitz continuity and \(u(0)=0\) also
give \(|u(x)|\leq -x\).  Hence
\[
 |u(x)|\leq\phi(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in[-1,1].
\]
Both \(\phi\) and \(-\phi\) are continuous, bounded by one, globally
one-Lipschitz, and satisfy the support obstacle: on the first rectangle their
absolute value is at most \(1/2\leq |z|\), and on the second they vanish.
Thus \(\phi,-\phi\in\mathcal C_{P^{\circ}}\).

On the first rectangle \(S=1\), while on the second rectangle the conditional
mean of \(S\) given \(X\) is zero by symmetry.  The definition of \(\nu_P\)
therefore gives
\[
 d\nu_{P^{\circ}}(x)
 =p_{\circ}\mathbf 1\{x\in[-1,0]\}\,dx.
\]
It follows from the pointwise envelope above that
\[
 -\frac{3p_{\circ}}8
 \leq J_{P^{\circ}}(u)
 \leq \frac{3p_{\circ}}8,
\]
and the lower and upper bounds are attained by \(-\phi\) and \(\phi\),
respectively.  Since \(T=0\) and
\(A=(1+5p_{\circ})/8\), \(\text{thm:full-law-sharpness}\) and the already
established \(\text{thm:attained-interval}\) imply
\[
 \Theta(P^{\circ})=
 \left[-\frac{3p_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}},
        \frac{3p_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}}\right].
\]
The constructions show \(Q_+^{\circ}=Q_1^{\circ}\) and
\(Q_-^{\circ}=Q_{-1}^{\circ}\).  The formula for \(\theta(Q_c^{\circ})\)
therefore shows that these laws attain the lower and upper endpoints,
respectively.

Finally, under baseline-conditional zero support, \((x,0)\in H\) for every
relevant \(x\).  The obstacle defining \(\mathcal C_P\) then gives
\[
 |g(x,0)-u(x)|\leq K|0|=0,
\]
so every compatible trend satisfies \(u(x)=g(x,0)\).  Substitution into
\(\text{def:waoss-set}\) reduces the bounded-class identified set to the
singleton
\[
 \left\{\frac{T-\int_{X_0}g(x,0)\,d\nu_P(x)}{A}\right\}.
\]
Thus the unrestricted published class yields all of \(\mathbb R\) at this
regular witness, the strengthened bounded-slope/Lipschitz sensitivity class
yields the finite displayed interval, and baseline-conditional zero support
collapses the obstacle set to the weighted singleton.  Only the negative
failure of the published singleton transfers to the unrestricted source class;
the finite sensitivity interval does not.
